chats.answer:
The NuPhy Air65 V3 is my pick for the best 65% low-profile mechanical keyboard for most people. It keeps dedicated arrow keys, has a comfortable gasket-mounted typing feel, and offers Bluetooth, 2.4GHz wireless and USB-C. Its 3.5 mm switch travel also gives it a more substantial mechanical feel than many slim keyboards. 
RTINGS.com
+1

The three I'd consider

NuPhy Air65 V3

$129.95

NuPhy · 4.5/5 (140)

Best overall. Soft gasket mount, hot-swappable switches and versatile wireless connectivity. The flat keycaps may take adjustment, and their legends don't shine through. 
RTINGS.com

Lofree Flow 2 68 — Pulse switches

$139.00

Lofree | Fun 2㎡ Designer for Mechanical Keyboard · 4.6/5 (20)

Best premium typing pick. CNC-aluminum case, refined keystrokes and shine-through legends. I'd favor this for writing and coding over competitive gaming. 
RTINGS.com

Keychron K7 Pro

$73.49

Keychron · 5/5 (2)

Best for programmable layouts. QMK/VIA remapping, Bluetooth and USB-C. Check the configuration if you want hot-swappable switches; not every version has them.

Which would I buy? The NuPhy for mixed work and gaming; the Lofree if typing feel and an aluminum case matter more. I assumed you want a conventional, ready-to-use wireless keyboard with arrow keys and no function row, rather than a gaming-specific magnetic-switch board. The independent lab comparisons cited above tested larger variants of these keyboard families, not each exact 65% model, so the typing comparisons aren't direct head-to-head tests of these three sizes.

NuPhy

68 keys, gasket mount, hot-swappable switches, RGB, and Bluetooth/2.4GHz/USB-C. A versatile choice for work and gaming, with linear, tactile, and silent switch options. The key legends aren't backlit.

CNC aluminum case, cushioned gasket mount, stable lubricated switches, shine-through keycaps, and VIA remapping. My choice for a premium desk keyboard; heavier to carry, with white-only backlighting.

Keychron K7 Pro — Lower-cost alternative

$73.49

Keychron

A straightforward slim 65% board with QMK/VIA programming, Bluetooth, and USB-C. No 2.4GHz wireless; check the configuration if you want hot-swappable switches.

What I’d buy: the Lofree with linear switches for a home-office desk, or the NuPhy if I regularly moved between locations. Both retain dedicated arrow keys without a function row.
